title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm to enhance large language models (LLMs) by conditioning generation on external evidence retrieved at inference time. The survey organizes RAG systems into four architectural categories: retriever-centric, generator-centric, hybrid, and robustness-oriented approaches, analyzing improvements in retrieval optimization, context filtering, and efficiency, then evaluating these on question-answering benchmarks. Key findings highlight recurring trade-offs between retrieval precision and generation flexibility, efficiency and faithfulness, and modularity and coordination. The work concludes by identifying emerging research areas including adaptive retrieval, real-time integration, multi-hop reasoning, and privacy-aware mechanisms for future RAG development.
